title: The Court Singer and the Caliph

keywords: the court singer and the caliph
full_text:
A celebrated court singer named Ibrahim was performing before Caliph Harun al-Rashid in a banquet hall glowing with crystal lamps and overflowing with rare delicacies.

While the courtiers praised the luxury of the feast, Ibrahim looked out through the marble colonnade and saw a line of impoverished laborers shivering in the cold midnight rain outside the palace walls.

Instead of singing another song of royal flattery, Ibrahim touched the strings of his lute and sang an impassioned, soulful ballad:
'The feast is warm within the gilded hall,
While winter rains upon the humble fall;
Remember, King, the bread that feeds thy state
Is gathered by the hands outside thy gate!'

The courtiers gasped at his bold verse, but Harun al-Rashid was pierced to his soul with remorse.

The Caliph ordered the banquet dishes carried out to feed the shivering laborers, distributed five thousand dinars to the city poor, and established public soup-kitchens, rewarding the brave singer for reminding power of its duty to the weak.
moral: Artistic voices should champion the cause of the vulnerable before the thrones of the mighty.
